name: Dishon
overview: Dishon was a male Edomite, identified uniquely as the son of Anah according to Genesis 36:25. The biblical record situates him within the Edomite lineage, emphasizing his tribal affiliation without additional personal details or narrative events.
namesAndTitles: The name Dishon is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 36:25 and is thought to mean 'ibex,' referring to a type of wild goat. This name was not given by God but reflects a common naming practice of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Dishon is explicitly recorded as the father of Beeri in Genesis 36:25. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran as noted in Genesis 36:26. These relationships place him as a patriarchal figure within the Edomite genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Dishon’s significance lies primarily in his role within the Edomite genealogical records, which trace the descendants of Esau. As the son of Anah and father to several sons, he contributes to the lineage that defines the Edomite tribal structure. Although not central to major biblical events, his mention helps preserve the historical and familial context important for understanding the broader biblical narrative of Edom.
